## SegmentedControl<T> — inventory & design rationale

### The divergent vocabularies found
Five real single-select segmented controls exist today, in two camps:

| Caller | Wrapper | Active fill | Role / a11y | Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ScaleToggle` | bordered (`overflow-hidden rounded border`) | `bg-ink text-paper` ✅ | group / aria-pressed | text-xs px-3 py-1.5, `flex-1` |
| `RepresentationToggle` | bordered | `bg-ink text-paper` ✅ | group / aria-pressed | text-xs px-3 py-1.5 |
| `GroupingModeToggle` | plain (`gap-1`, no border) | `bg-ink text-paper` ✅ | radiogroup / radio+aria-checked | text-xs px-1.5 py-0.5 |
| `AnnotationToggles` | plain | **`bg-paper-sunk text-ink`** ❌ (L-5/B-A defect) | group / aria-pressed | text-xs px-1.5 py-0.5 |
| `PlotCard.XScaleToggle` | bordered + manual `w-px` divider | **`bg-paper-sunk text-ink`** ❌ | **none** (no role, no aria-pressed) | text-xs px-1.5 py-0.5 |

Plus two page-level uses that share the active fill but live inline: `CorpusTopbar` view-seg (route-driven Link/span/disabled-button hybrid) and `SeriesFolioPage` sort (bordered, `text-[11.5px] font-semibold`) + filter chips (`rounded-full` pills).

### Canonical look (DESIGN.md §206/§211/§240)
Active segment = **ink fill + paper text**. The recessed `bg-paper-sunk` fill on AnnotationToggles and XScaleToggle is named the L-5/B-A defect in §211 ("the active state must not read as a recessed fill") — the primitive converges everyone to `bg-ink text-paper`, and `bg-paper-sunk` is demoted to a hover/ghost affordance only. Rest state: `text-ink-faint`/`text-ink-soft` on transparent.

### Two variants, one active vocabulary
- **bordered** — `inline-flex overflow-hidden rounded border border-hair-strong` wrapper, segments butt edge-to-edge; XScaleToggle's hand-rolled `w-px` divider becomes a built-in inter-segment hairline. Covers ScaleToggle, RepresentationToggle, XScaleToggle, folio sort, (and view-seg if Link-segments are supported).
- **plain** — no wrapper border, `gap-1` between pill segments (`rounded` per segment). Covers GroupingModeToggle.

Follows the `Button.tsx` pattern exactly: a `Record<Variant,string>` class map, base classes first, consumer `className` appended for PLACEMENT only, typed props. A tiny local `cx()` join helper is acceptable (no `cx` exists today — buttons use `.join(" ")` / template strings). No cva/clsx/tailwind-merge.

### Active-fill convergence is the payoff
Migrating AnnotationToggles and XScaleToggle is the main behavioral/visual delta: both move off the banned recessed fill to ink-on-paper. XScaleToggle additionally gains the missing `role="group"` + `aria-pressed` it lacks today.

### What the catalog must show
- Both variants (bordered, plain) at both sizes (sm, md).
- 2-option and 3-option instances (log/linear; bySample/byPhase/distinct).
- States: a selected segment (ink-on-paper), unselected (faint), hover, focus-visible ring, and a per-segment `disabled` (the Loupe case).
- Both roles: `group`+aria-pressed and `radiogroup`+aria-checked, to show the semantic switch.
- The 44px touch-target treatment side-by-side with the dense desktop density, so the resolution of the open question is visible.

### a11y the primitive owns / preserves
- `role` prop drives child semantics: `group` -> button[`aria-pressed`]; `radiogroup` -> button[`role=radio`][`aria-checked`].
- Required `aria-label` on the container (XScaleToggle and folio-sort lack one today — this fixes it).
- `focus-visible` outline on each segment (currently absent on most).
- Touch target: fold in `min-h-[44px]` per the brief (mechanism is an open question — unconditional vs `pointer:coarse` vs a density flag).
- Preserve every existing `data-testid`, plus `data-active`/`data-value` per segment and a container state attr; honor GroupingModeToggle's `data-mode` and CorpusTopbar's `aria-current`.

### Test plan (Vitest — RENDERED SEMANTICS only, never class strings)
1. Renders one button per option with the correct accessible name (label text).
2. The option matching `value` exposes the selected semantic: `aria-pressed="true"` (group) / `aria-checked="true"` (radiogroup); others false. Assert via `getByRole("radio",{checked:true})` etc.
3. Clicking an unselected segment fires `onChange(value)` once with that value; clicking the active segment behavior per spec (re-fire or no-op — decide).
4. `disabled` segment is not clickable and exposes `aria-disabled`/`disabled`.
5. Container carries the required `aria-label` and the role passed.
6. `data-active`/`data-value`/container state attr reflect `value` (asserted as attributes, not classes) — this is the E2E contract.
7. Keyboard: Tab focuses; for radiogroup, Arrow keys move selection (if roving nav is adopted) — gated on the open question.
8. Guard/lint companion: a consumer `className` containing an appearance utility is rejected (covered by the Phase-0 guard, referenced here).
9. Generic typing: `SegmentedControl<ScaleMode>` rejects an option/value outside the union at compile time (type-level test or tsc).

### Migration shape (representative)
Each existing component either deletes down to a one-line wrapper around the primitive (keeping its public `value`/`onChange` props and exported union type so importers like the figure-export adapters and SeriesBuilderPage are untouched) or, for the page-level inline ones (folio sort, view-seg), the inline JSX is replaced in place by `<SegmentedControl … options={OPTIONS} />`, mapping each existing `data-testid` onto `option.testId`.

## What PhaseChip is (and is not)

PhaseChip is the **monospace, phase-tinted data badge that names a phase** (DESIGN.md line 226). Only **two** live sites are true phase chips: `SampleStatusChip` (the M-6 contact-sheet status cell) and `MemberMetaRow`'s `member-meta-phase-chip`. Everything else the grep surfaced that renders a phase name with `phaseColor()` is a *different* pattern and must NOT be folded in:

- **Colored phase text without a surface** (PhasePanel:141 candidate-row label, PhasePanel:42 serif title, FocusReflectionsTable:178 dot-label) — these pair the hue with another second channel (score bar, dot, row state). Adding a tint surface would over-decorate and contradict the rationing intent. They belong to a future `PhaseLabel`/`SemanticDot` discussion, not this wave.
- **The SpeculativeBuilder `anchor` badge** (243) — renders the literal word "anchor", not a phase name. PhaseChip's contract is "always render the phase name," so it structurally cannot represent this. Separate one-off tag.
- **SeriesFolioCard swatches** (116) and the phase **strips** (ScopingPhaseStrip, SeriesPhaseStrip, ScopingSparkline) — these are the **PhaseStrip** sibling primitive's territory: colored cells/gradients, name only in tooltips.

This narrowing matters: the brief's "always render the name" requirement is exactly why the chip can't absorb the anchor tag or the strips.

## API rationale

- **`phase` is a domain prop, not a color.** Following the ScoreBar lesson in the brief (raw `color` → `phase`), PhaseChip owns `phaseColor(phase)` + the `color-mix` recipe internally. No consumer passes a raw color string. This kills the three hand-rolled `color-mix(in oklab, ${color} N%, transparent)` copies.
- **`variant: 'tint' | 'solid'`.** Tint is the canonical M-6 look (phase-colored text on a faint phase-tinted fill). `solid` (phase fill + `text-paper`) is added for high-emphasis/dense contexts and to give the catalog a second state; if no current site needs solid, it still earns its place as the obvious second variant and prevents future ad-hoc inline solid chips. (Open question: confirm a real solid consumer or keep it speculative.)
- **`size: 'sm' | 'md'`.** Resolves the real divergence: SampleStatusChip is 11px (`sm`), MemberMetaRow is `text-data-strong`/13px (`md`). Two sizes, no more — Fixed-Scale.
- **`className` placement-only**, appended last, documented and guarded. MemberMetaRow's `shrink-0` is the one real placement utility in use and is legal.

## Canonical values to bake in
- Tint fill: **13%** (`color-mix(in oklab, ${color} 13%, transparent)`) — the M-6 value; normalizes MemberMetaRow's 10% up by 3% (imperceptible, 1-channel).
- Tint border: **35%** — keep MemberMetaRow's border; add it to the SampleStatusChip look (benign legibility win on AA-tuned hues).
- Radius: **`rounded-sm` (5px)** per DESIGN.md line 205; normalizes SampleStatusChip's 4px up by 1px.
- Text: `phaseColor(phase)` foreground, `font-mono font-bold`.

## What the two files actually share vs diverge

Identical (internalize verbatim):
- The gradient: `linear-gradient(100deg, ${phaseColor(A)} 42%, ${phaseColor(B)} 58%)` — byte-for-byte in both.
- Single-phase fill: `phaseColor(phase)`.
- Segment shape: `flex-1 rounded-[1.5px]`, flex row.
- Caption logic: first non-null phase, last non-null phase, "throughout" when they agree (Scoping: `first===last`; Series via `buildPhaseStrip`: `distinct.size === 1`). NOTE a subtle semantic difference below.

Divergent (must reconcile):
1. Unindexed fill — Scoping `var(--color-hair)` (oklch 0.882, very pale) vs Series `var(--color-ink-faint)` (oklch 0.640). SeriesMiniWaterfall.tsx:40 uses `--color-hair` only for the axis rule and `UNINDEXED_COLOR = var(--color-ink-faint)` (folioFigure.ts:107) for unindexed traces. Canonical = `--color-ink-faint`.

3. Caption "throughout" definition — Scoping says "throughout" whenever `first===last` (FIRST and LAST agree, ignoring the middle). Series says "throughout" only when `distinct.size === 1` (ALL indexed segments are one phase). Example: [Pn3m, Lamellar, Pn3m] -> Scoping prints "Pn3m throughout"; Series prints "transition" (because distinct={Pn3m,Lamellar}). The primitive must pick ONE. Recommend the Series semantic (distinct-count) — it is the truthful one; "throughout" implying uniformity while the middle differs is a small lie. This is a behavioral change for Scoping; see Open Questions.
4. Leading heading — Scoping has an uppercase kicker; Series has none. -> optional `heading` prop.
5. Empty copy — "Members not yet indexed; phase preview unavailable." vs "No clear phase". -> `emptyLabel` prop.
6. Arrow a11y — Series marks the "→" `aria-hidden="true"`; Scoping does not. Canonical = aria-hidden (it is decorative; the phase names carry meaning).
7. testids — `scoping-ps-seg`/`scoping-ps-cap` vs `series-phase-strip`/`ps-seg`/`ps-cap`. Canonical = `ps-seg`/`ps-cap` (+ optional container `phase-strip`).

## Kicker — API rationale

`Kicker` is the smallest possible primitive: it owns ONE thing the audit flagged ~37 times — the uppercase, letter-spaced, small "eyebrow/label" treatment — and routes it through the existing `.text-label` typography role so geometry lives in ONE place (styles.css). It adds only a `tone` switch for the two color families that actually exist in the wild (terracotta `print-accent` page/section eyebrows; dim `ink-faint` metric/field/aside labels). It does NOT reintroduce per-site `text-[Npx]`, `tracking-[…]`, or `font-bold/semibold` — those are the Fixed-Scale violations the extraction is meant to kill.

### Why fold SectionLabel in
`SectionLabel` is literally `<h3 className="text-label mb-2">` and (per grep) has no live importers beyond the barrel re-export (`ui/index.ts:7`). It is a strict subset of Kicker: same role, fixed tone (ink-soft/faint), fixed element (h3), fixed margin. Kicker generalizes it with `tone` + `as` + placement-only `className`. Recommend: keep a 1-line `SectionLabel` alias (`<Kicker as="h3" className="mb-2" {...p}/>`) ONLY if external imports are expected; otherwise delete it and migrate to Kicker directly. The barrel must export `Kicker` either way.

### The two tones (and the lurking third)
- `accent` → `text-print-accent`: page/section eyebrows — "Folio", "Contact sheet", "Integration", series-builder section headers, SeriesFolioCard eyebrow, SeriesScopingPage section label. Currently rendered wide-tracked (0.13–0.14em) and bold; standardizes to 0.06em/500.
- `faint` → `text-ink-faint`: metric sublabels ("samples screened", "series in the folio"), scoping field labels, "Sort", "Notes", "Offset", "sample N of M", PhasePanel section labels.
- **Lurking third (`ink`)**: `SeriesRecipeEditor:131` ("Recipe", text-ink), `FocusDetectorPanel:98` ("Detector image", text-meta/ink), `FocusReflectionsTable:230` ("Reflections", text-meta/ink). These are full-ink card-header labels. The brief specifies only `accent|faint`. Resolution needed (openQuestions) — either a third tone or leave un-migrated. Do NOT silently dim them to faint.

### Explicit EXCLUSIONS (look like kickers, aren't)
- `LoupeFrame:56` "Dropped" badge — `text-paper` on `bg-print-accent`; a Badge/Chip, not a kicker.
- `FocusDetectorPanel:151` "Set rep" / `CorpusTopbar:133,153` nav tabs — interactive button labels (Button/SegmentedControl).
- `CorpusTopbar:99` HIMALAYA wordmark — brand identity, ink, widest tracking, a home link.
- `FocusReflectionsTable:120,125` — `font-mono` table headers; mono is appearance and banned in className, so they cannot be a plain Kicker.

### `className` contract (placement only)
Allowed: `mb-2`, `mb-1.5`, `mt-0.5`, `mt-1`, `mt-5`, `ml-auto`, `block`, `px-4 pt-2.5`, and the transform/position stack on the rotated axis title (`absolute left-0 top-1/2 origin-left -translate-y-1/2 -rotate-90 whitespace-nowrap pointer-events-none z-10`). Banned (now flows through props/role): `uppercase`, `tracking-*`, `text-[Npx]`, `text-xs/sm`, `font-bold/semibold`, `text-print-accent`, `text-ink-faint`, `text-ink`, `text-meta`, `text-label`. The Phase 0 guard baseline should record every banned-utility occurrence at the call sites above.

### Catalog must show
- Both tones side by side (accent vs faint) at the single scale, on a `--color-plate` swatch.
- A true section heading example (`as="h3"`) vs an inline aside (`as="span"`).
- A kicker+serif-title pair (the dominant pattern: Kicker over a `text-display`/`text-headline`), to prove the eyebrow→title rhythm.
- The placement-override example: a kicker with `mb-2` and one with `ml-auto`.
- (If `ink` tone is approved) the third tone for card-header labels.

### Test plan (rendered semantics, NEVER class strings)
- Renders children text: `getByText("Integration")` present.
- tone wiring asserted via SEMANTICS not classes: render `<Kicker tone="accent">` and `<Kicker tone="faint">` and assert they are distinguishable through a `data-tone` attribute the component sets (recommend adding `data-tone={tone}` so tests assert `toHaveAttribute("data-tone","accent")` instead of reading Tailwind classes — keeps within the anti-pattern rule).
- `as="h3"` produces a heading: `getByRole("heading", { name: "Folio" })`.
- Default element is non-heading (div) for inline labels: heading role ABSENT when `as` omitted.
- Forwards `data-testid`: `<Kicker data-testid="focus-plot-kicker">` → `getByTestId("focus-plot-kicker")` (guards FocusPlotHeader migration).
- Forwards `aria-hidden`: `<Kicker aria-hidden="true">` → `toHaveAttribute("aria-hidden","true")` (guards the heatmap axis title).
- Accepts placement className: `<Kicker className="mb-2">` → element has the class (allowed since margin is placement) — this is the ONE acceptable class assertion, scoped to proving className pass-through, not appearance.
- Migration guard test (Phase 3): a lint/guard asserts no inline `uppercase` + `tracking-` + small-size combo remains in the migrated files.

### Recommended `data-tone` addition
To keep Vitest off Tailwind strings, have Kicker emit `data-tone={tone}`. This gives tests and the eventual guard a semantic handle and costs nothing.

DESIGN.md §Flat-Except-the-Plate / §Elevation: the single lifted object is the plate; a modal IS a lifted surface (it carries the Plate-Lift shadow), so it must be `plate`, not `paper`.

## useFocusTrap textarea fix (load-bearing)

`FOCUSABLE` (useFocusTrap.ts:3) omits `textarea`. The Notes drawer (FocusWorkspaceLayout.tsx:149) is a `role=dialog aria-modal` whose body (`FocusNotesMargin`, textarea at line 108) is its primary — often only — interactive element. With textarea excluded, `focusable` can be empty (trap no-ops, line 24 early-return) or compute the wrong first/last, so Tab escapes the drawer. Fix per brief: add `textarea:not([disabled])`; also add `a[href]` (links are focusable and the onboarding/tutorial copy could contain them) for completeness — flag the anchor addition as optional if the spec author wants the minimal diff. Consumers of useFocusTrap (all migrate transitively into ModalShell, but the hook stays public): ConflictModalShell:53, FocusWorkspaceLayout:44, NavModal:78, SpeculativeBuilder:39, ScopingConfirmModal:21, OnboardingFlow:201 & 314.

## API rationale

- **`open` gate** — every site already does `if (!open) return null` (or is parent-mount-gated). Centralizing it means ModalShell returns null when closed, so the focus-trap/Esc effects never arm — matches today.
- **`size` token** — three observed widths (820/640/420-ish) collapse to lg/md/sm. Keeps the `w-[min(Npx,calc(100vw-48px))]` clamp that ConflictModalShell/NavModal already use; sm tier standardizes the ad-hoc max-w-md / min-w-[360px] / p-6 boxes.
- **`align`** — only NavModal wants top placement (command-palette feel, pt-[12vh]); everyone else centers. A two-value prop avoids a className appearance leak.
- **`closeOnEsc` / `closeOnOutsideClick`** — NavModal owns Esc in its input handler; OnboardingFlow must not dismiss on backdrop click. Defaults (true/true) fit the majority; the two exceptions pass false.
- **`variant=\"drawer\"`** — the Notes drawer is a right-edge sheet with a lower-z scrim and slide-in, not a centered box. One primitive keeps trap/Esc/scrim single-sourced (see open question on a separate DrawerShell).
- **`testId`** — forwarded to the frame; scrim gets `${testId}-scrim` to preserve FocusWorkspaceLayout's existing `focus-notes-drawer-scrim` id.
- **a11y passthrough** — `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` forwarded to the frame; runtime/dev assert at least one is present (ConflictModalShell uses labelledby+describedby; others use label).

## Internals (class-map pattern, no new deps)

```ts
const sizeClass: Record<ModalSize,string> = {
  sm: "w-[min(440px,calc(100vw-48px))]",
  md: "w-[min(640px,calc(100vw-48px))]",
  lg: "w-[min(820px,calc(100vw-48px))]",
};
const alignClass: Record<ModalAlign,string> = {
  center: "items-center justify-center",
  top:    "items-start justify-center pt-[12vh]",
};
// scrim (dialog): `fixed inset-0 z-50 flex bg-scrim backdrop-blur-sm anim-pal-in ${alignClass}`
// frame (dialog): `bg-plate border border-hair-strong rounded-xl shadow-2xl anim-pal-scale flex flex-col overflow-hidden ${className}`
// drawer scrim:   `fixed inset-0 z-40 bg-scrim`  (NOTE: lower z, may keep ink/20-weight scrim — decide via scrim token)
// drawer frame:   `fixed right-0 top-14 bottom-0 z-50 w-[300px] max-w-[85vw] overflow-y-auto bg-plate border-l border-hair-strong shadow-xl`
```
`bg-scrim` depends on the Phase-0 `--color-scrim` token (the repeated `oklch(0.05_0_0/0.65)` literal). Until that lands, ModalShell can inline the literal once. A tiny local `cx(...parts)` join helper is acceptable (brief allows it); no cva/clsx/tailwind-merge.

## Catalog states to show

Scrim + frame at each size (sm/md/lg); align center vs top; dialog vs drawer variant; a long-content frame demonstrating internal scroll (max-h + overflow); closeOnEsc/closeOnOutsideClick toggles (interactive); a frame whose only focusable is a textarea (proves the useFocusTrap fix). Show the anim-pal entry once.

## Test plan (rendered-semantics only, never class strings)

1. **Open gate** — `open={false}` renders nothing (`queryByRole('dialog')` null); `open` renders a `role=dialog` with `aria-modal=true`.
2. **a11y label** — the frame exposes the passed `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`; the dialog is the accessible node (regression guard for the SpeculativeBuilder role-on-scrim bug — assert role=dialog is NOT on the backdrop).
3. **Esc** — with `closeOnEsc` (default), firing `keydown Escape` calls `onClose`; with `closeOnEsc={false}`, it does not.
4. **Outside click** — clicking the scrim (the `${testId}-scrim` node / `e.target===currentTarget`) calls `onClose`; clicking inside the frame does not; with `closeOnOutsideClick={false}` neither does.
5. **Focus trap** — Tab from the last focusable wraps to the first and vice-versa (port useFocusTrap.test.tsx pattern); ADD a textarea-only case so the FOCUSABLE fix is locked.
6. **Focus restore** — focus returns to the previously-focused trigger on close (already in useFocusTrap.test.tsx:67).
7. **testId forwarding** — frame gets `testId`, scrim gets `${testId}-scrim`.
8. **Drawer variant** — renders the right-edge sheet, scrim at the lower z (assert via the testid'd nodes, not z-class strings — i.e. assert structure/role, not the class).
9. **Per-site migration tests stay green** — NavModal.test / SpeculativeBuilder.test / Scoping*.test / ConflictModalShell.test / SeriesCommitConflictModal.test keep asserting role/aria/testid/text against the same nodes.

detailMarkdown:
## Card / Plate

### Why `elevated?` is the only axis
DESIGN.md establishes exactly two surface kinds in the paper world: the **flat hairline card** (tonal + hairline separation, no shadow) and the **single lifted Plate** (the "Plate Lift" recipe). The named rule (DESIGN.md:200) is categorical: "A drop shadow on anything else is wrong." So a boolean `elevated` is the correct API surface, not a 3-step elevation scale. Default MUST be `false` because the grep shows ~28 bg-plate surfaces and only **four families** are truly the lifted plate (figure plate, folio cards, scoping worksheet, builder worksheet — DESIGN.md:196) plus a small set of legitimately-floating objects (popover menu, offset dock, dropdown) that float above the page and earn a shadow by being detached, not by being "the plate."

### The single source of truth for the shadow
The Plate Lift shadow already lives in the `.card` CSS rule (styles.css:172). `elevated` should reuse that class rather than re-inlining the box-shadow, so there is exactly one place the recipe is defined. The two inline worksheet shadows (SeriesScopingPage:236, SeriesBuilderPage:277) and the OffsetDock shadow (:20) are **drift** — three different warm drop-shadow recipes. The spec must decide whether to: (a) collapse all to `.card`'s recipe, or (b) keep a `deep` worksheet/floater variant. My recommendation: collapse worksheets to `.card`; treat floating objects (dock, popover, dropdown menu) as a separate `floating` concern or a `Popover` primitive — they are not "cards" semantically.

### Radius reconciliation (must resolve before build)
- `.card` hardcodes `border-radius: 12px` and `border: 0.5px`.
- DESIGN.md:214 says cards are **7px** (`rounded.md`) with a `hair-strong` hairline.
- Inline sites variously use `rounded` (4px), `rounded-md` (6px via `--radius`), `rounded-lg`, `rounded-xl`.
This is a genuine Fixed-Scale violation cluster. Phase 0 adds `rounded.sm`/`rounded.md` tokens; Card must adopt `rounded-md` and a consistent border, which means **changing `.card`'s 12px → 7px** — a deliberate visual change the spec must sign off on (it touches the figure plate, the most prominent surface).

### Surfaces that are NOT cards (route elsewhere — flagged in callSites)
The bg-plate grep over-captures. These match `bg-plate + border + rounded` but are other primitives:
- **Inputs / value wells:** ScopingOrderField:21, ScopingValueCell:50, CorpusTopbar:177 (select) → Input (DESIGN.md:218 recessed input).
- **Buttons / chips:** ScopingLooseMatches:60, PlotCard:511, CorpusTopbar:299, ScopingLooseMatches → Button; tag pills (LoupeSidebar:118/135, ContactSheetRow:422/439, SamplesPage:215) → a Chip/Tag primitive.
- **Banners (Phase 3):** StaleIndicesBanner:66, InfrastructureBanner:45-46 → status-icon+label banner concern.
- **Modal shells (Phase 2 sibling):** NavModal:227, ConflictModalShell:85, OnboardingFlow:226/325, SpeculativeBuilder:124 → ModalShell. Note these use `shadow-2xl`/`shadow-xl` (Tailwind defaults), which are Flat-Except-the-Plate violations to fix inside ModalShell, not Card.
- **Segmented container (Phase 1):** CorpusTopbar:213 → SegmentedControl.
- **Tooltip / ink toolbar:** MultiTracePlot:679 (bare `shadow`), CullBar:26 (bg-ink + drop shadow) → ephemeral floaters; CullBar is explicitly bg-ink, not a plate.

### Catalog must show
flat card (border=hair), flat card (border=strong), elevated plate, elevated next to flat (to demonstrate the depth contrast), and a "wrong" example annotation (flat card must have NO shadow). Show the figure-plate at its real width to validate the 7px radius decision.

### Test plan (rendered semantics, never class strings)
- `elevated` renders a `data-elevated="true"` attribute (add one) → assert `toHaveAttribute`, not the box-shadow class.
- flat default does NOT carry `data-elevated`.
- children render; `className` placement passes through (assert via a placement marker like a custom data-attr or that a passed `data-testid` lands on the root, not by asserting `bg-plate`).
- guard-side: a snapshot/lint test that consumer `className` contains no `bg-`, `border-`, `shadow-`, `rounded-` tokens (the Phase 0 guard baseline owns this; Card just must not regress it).

---

## IconButton

### The problem this fixes
Eleven+ icon-only buttons, each hand-rolling padding (`px-1`/`px-0.5`/`px-1.5`/`px-2`/`p-1`), color (`text-ink-soft` vs `text-ink-faint`), hover (`hover:text-ink` vs `hover:text-error` vs `hover:text-print-accent`), and glyph (`×` U+00D7 vs `×` vs `✕` U+2715). Critically, **only PhasePanel:163 has the accent focus-visible ring** DESIGN.md:209 mandates; every other icon button is keyboard-invisible on focus. Two (SeriesRecipeEditor reorder + remove) have **no aria-label at all** (only `title`), so they are unnamed to screen readers.

### Standardization decisions
- **Hit area:** `min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` + `inline-flex items-center justify-center` gives a 44px touch target (WCAG 2.5.5) while the glyph stays visually compact. This is a behavior change at dense sites (chip removes inside tag pills) — see risks.
- **Focus ring:** the canonical accent ring from PhasePanel:163 (`focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-accent`).
- **aria-label REQUIRED** via the `label` prop (typed as required; `aria-label` is `Omit`ted from the spread so callers can't bypass it). `title` defaults to `label`.
- **Canonical dismiss glyph:** `×` (U+00D7) via `dismiss` prop. The heavier `✕` (U+2715) at SeriesRecipeEditor:171 normalizes to ×. The grease-pencil reject **✕ on detector frames** (ContactSheetRow:50, LoupeFrame:48, CrossTraceTrackingLayer:124) is a DOMAIN mark, explicitly NOT an IconButton — leave those alone.
- **tone:** `ghost` (hover→ink) default; `danger` (hover→error) for delete/remove. Open question: three tag-remove sites use `hover:text-print-accent` (the accent alias), not error — the spec must pick one dismiss-hover convention (I lean accent for "remove this chip" since DESIGN.md:121 makes the terracotta accent the reject/grease-pencil mark; `danger`=error reserved for destructive delete like PhasePanel spec-delete).

### Non-dismiss icon buttons
IconButton is not dismiss-only. Steppers (CorpusTopbar prev/next, `‹`/`›`) and recipe reorder (`▲`/`▼`) are `children`-glyph IconButtons with `disabled` support (the primitive includes `disabled:opacity-30 disabled:cursor-not-allowed`, already present at those sites).

### Catalog must show
ghost dismiss (×), danger dismiss, ghost with custom glyph (chevron), with-SVG-child (trash), disabled, and a focus-ring screenshot (Tab to it). Show it inside a tight chip to validate the 44px target doesn't blow out dense rows.

### Test plan (rendered semantics)
- `label` → assert `getByRole("button", { name })` resolves (covers both the missing-aria sites once migrated).
- `dismiss` → asserts the accessible name comes from `label`, and textContent is `×` (U+00D7), NOT a class.
- `tone="danger"` vs ghost → assert via a `data-tone` attribute (add one) rather than the hover class.
- `disabled` → `toBeDisabled()` and click handler not fired.
- focus ring is class-based so it is NOT asserted (per the repo anti-pattern) — instead a Playwright/axe a11y check that the focused element has a visible outline, if desired.
- migration regression: each existing `data-testid` (`focus-notes-drawer-close`, `${testId}-remove`, `spec-delete-*`, `recipe-row-remove/up/down`, `sample-stepper-prev/next`) must still resolve after the swap — these are queried in existing specs.
migrationRisks: 44px min hit area is a BEHAVIORAL/visual change at dense sites: the chip-remove × inside tag pills (LoupeSidebar:126/179, ContactSheetRow:431/438) and the NavModal Chip remove (:339) live in compact rows; forcing min-w/min-h 44px on the BUTTON box could blow out pill height. Likely need the 44px to be a hit-area (pseudo-element / negative margin) rather than a layout box, OR a size variant for in-chip use. Resolve before adopting.

Three tag-remove buttons hover to `text-print-accent` (the accent alias added in Phase 0), not text-error. If IconButton danger=hover:text-error, those lose the accent-hover the design intends. Pick the dismiss-hover convention explicitly.

SeriesRecipeEditor remove (:171) uses ✕ (U+2715) and reorder buttons (:152/:162) have NO aria-label (only title). ## Adopt-or-delete verdicts (Phase 0)

| Primitive | Importers (grep) | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Button** | 3 files, 6 JSX usages (SpeculativeBuilder, StaleIndicesBanner, OnboardingFlow) | **ADOPT + fix** | Live + correct shape, but leaks `text-white` and mis-assigns the solid color. |
| **HintText** | 5 files import + 1 barrel (6 total), 14 JSX usages | **ADOPT as-is** | Correct, widely used empty/loading caption voice. |
| **Toast / ToastContainer** | 1 (App.tsx, via deep path) | **ADOPT, fix barrel** | Works; just not exported from `index.ts`. Stripe fix is Phase 3, not now. |
| **ScoreBar** | **0** | **ADOPT by rewrite** | Dead, but the brief's target: it must serve the 2 inline phase bars; rewrite to `{value, phase, size}`. |
| **Dot** | **0** | **ADOPT by extend** | Dead, but 7 inline semantic dots want it; add `tone`+`size` to remove raw-class color leak. |
| **SectionLabel** | **0** | **DELETE** | Dead and no inline `text-label <h3>` call sites exist (the only `text-label` hits are the styles.css token + comment). Nothing to serve. |
| **Input** | **0** | **DELETE (defer real TextField)** | Dead; the 22 raw `<input>`s are mostly range/checkbox/radio (out of scope) and the text ones each carry bespoke adornment/borderless/stepper styling that a trivial wrapper can't absorb. A proper `TextField` is a later wave. |

### Confirmed: the `text-white` leak
`grep text-white` across the whole `src/` tree returns exactly ONE hit: `components/ui/Button.tsx:11` (the `primary` variant). Everywhere else that needs on-dark text already uses `text-paper` (e.g. PhasePanel checkbox mark at line 125, `text-paper`). So the fix is `text-white → text-paper`, and it is contained to this one file.

### The deeper Button finding (beyond the leak)
DESIGN.md §Buttons (lines 204-208, 240) defines the solid/confirm action as **ink fill + paper text** (`button-solid`), and reserves **terracotta fill + paper text** (`button-accent`) for the single grease-pencil action (reject, "+ New series"). The current `primary` variant is `bg-accent` (terracotta) — i.e. it uses the *accent* treatment for what are actually confirm/continue actions (Save, Re-analyze, Continue, Next, Done). The correct extraction renames the axis to `solid | accent | ghost | danger`, makes `solid` the ink-fill default-confirm and migrates all 4 `primary` sites to `solid`. This is a visual change (terracotta→ink) and must be called out, not slipped in.

### ScoreBar: the divergence and the fix
Three inline candidates, two are true score bars, one is a decoy:
- **PhasePanel:58** wide — `h-1 w-full bg-hair`, fill `background: phaseColor(phase)` → `size="bar"`.
- **PhasePanel:153** compact — `h-[3.5px] w-[46px] bg-hair` → `size="compact"` (the off-scale dims become a reviewed named size, satisfying the Fixed-Scale Rule).
- **SamplesPage:133** — `h-1 w-[152px] bg-hair` fill `bg-print-accent`, value=`pct` (samples screened). **This is a progress meter, not a score bar** — fixed accent, no phase. Excluded; future Meter primitive.

The dead primitive's own look (`h-0.5 w-full bg-paper-sunk mt-1`) matches NEITHER inline site (wrong height, wrong track color, baked-in margin) — proof it was never wired up. Rewrite drops it. New track is `bg-hair` (both real sites agree), `mt-*` becomes consumer placement.

### Dot: the inline census
Seven inline dots, varying on size (1.5 / 2 / 2.5), fill vs ring, and color source (Tailwind class vs inline style vs ternary). The adopt path adds:
- `tone`: accent (`bg-print-accent`), success (`bg-success`), neutral (`bg-hair-strong` / hollow ring), to replace the raw color classes/styles.
- `size`: xs (1.5), sm (2); decide on the lone 2.5 (LoupeSidebar:264).
- preserve `role="img"` + `label`, but allow `aria-hidden` decorative dots (CorpusTopbar pip, pager dots) to skip the label.
Each site's `data-testid`/`title` rides through `...props`.

### Catalog must show
- **Button:** all 4 variants × {rest, hover, focus-visible ring, disabled}; show solid is ink (not terracotta) and accent is terracotta; verify text reads as `paper`.
- **ScoreBar:** `bar` and `compact` sizes, several `phase` values (proving color derives from phase), and clamping at value=0 / 0.5 / 1 / out-of-range.
- **Dot:** every tone × size, plus the hollow/neutral ring and an aria-hidden decorative example.
- **HintText:** one example (italic faint caption).
- **Toast:** all four kinds (info/success/warning/error) with the side stripe + dismiss button (note: stripe convention changes in Phase 3).

### Test plan (Vitest — RENDERED SEMANTICS, never class strings)
- **Button:** renders a `button` with the children text; `variant` maps to `data-variant` (recommend adding a `data-variant` attr so tests assert semantics, not classes); disabled prop reflects `disabled` attribute; click fires `onClick`. Assert focus ring presence via the role, not the class.

- **Dot:** assert `role="img"` + `aria-label` present when `label` given; absent (aria-hidden) when decorative; assert a semantic `data-tone` reflects the tone prop. No class assertions.
- **Toast:** existing tests (role=status, data-toast-kind, dismiss aria-label) stay green; add a barrel-import smoke test (`import { ToastContainer } from "../components/ui"`).
- **Barrel:** a test importing every Phase-0 primitive from `components/ui` to lock the public surface (catches the Toast omission and any accidental re-add of Input/SectionLabel).

## (a) Token foundation — what `@theme` must add and WHY

**Radius is the load-bearing finding.** In Tailwind v4 the `rounded-*` utilities are generated from the `--radius-*` **namespace**, not the singular `--radius`. The repo defines only `--radius: 6px` (styles.css:65) and `var(--radius)` is referenced **nowhere** in `src/`. Net effect: `--radius: 6px` is **dead**, and today every `rounded-sm` / `rounded-md` / `rounded-lg` resolves to Tailwind's **stock defaults** (v4: `rounded-sm` 0.25rem/4px, `rounded-md` 0.375rem/6px, `rounded-lg` 0.5rem/8px, `rounded-xl` 0.75rem/12px), NOT the DESIGN.md `rounded: {sm:5px, md:7px}`. So the system has been shipping off-spec radii silently. The fix:

```css
--radius-sm:   5px;
--radius-md:   7px;
--radius-full: 9999px;   /* matches stock; pin for intent */
/* delete --radius: 6px */
```

After this, `rounded-sm`→5px and `rounded-md`→7px app-wide (33 `rounded-md` + 11 `rounded-sm` call sites silently snap to spec — a deliberate, reviewed visual change). **Bare `rounded` (185 occurrences)** is the catch: v4's bare `rounded` is its own default (0.25rem) independent of the `--radius-*` keys, so it does NOT pick up `--radius-sm`. The spec author must decide whether bare `rounded` is acceptable or should be linted toward `rounded-sm`/`rounded-md` (openQuestion). The `.card` rule hardcodes `border-radius:12px` (styles.css:175) — off the 5/7 scale; fold to `rounded-md` or a named `--radius-card`.

**Scrim.** Three modal backdrops inline the identical literal `bg-[oklch(0.05_0_0/0.65)]` (NavModal:217, ConflictModalShell:73, OnboardingFlow:147). Add `--color-scrim: oklch(0.05 0 0 / 0.65)` → use `bg-scrim`. Two other modals use stock `bg-black/40` (SpeculativeBuilder:118, ScopingConfirmModal:25) — a different value; decide whether to unify onto scrim.

**Accent de-dup.** `--color-print-accent` (styles.css:48) is a duplicated literal of `--color-accent` (styles.css:20). Alias it: `--color-print-accent: var(--color-accent)`. All `*-print-accent` utilities keep working, now value-identical by construction. (DESIGN.md: terracotta is "the only chrome hue" — one source.)

## (b) The guard — `scripts/check-design.mjs`

A zero-dep Node script (`.mjs`) that globs `packages/HimalayaUI/frontend/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`, **excludes `src/components/ui/**`** (primitives own appearance), reads each file, and flags banned patterns by line. Ban set:

1. **Inline arbitrary type size/color**: `/\btext-\[/` — bans both `text-[Npx]` (size) and `text-[<color>]`/`text-[var(--color-...)]` used as color (FocusNotesMargin:106). DESIGN.md Fixed-Scale Rule.
2. **Raw appearance color in a className color utility**: `/\b(bg|text|border|fill|stroke|ring|outline|from|via|to|decoration|shadow)-\[(?:[^\]]*?)(oklch|rgba?|#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}|hsla?)\b/` — but see scope notes: `shadow-[...rgba...]` elevation is **excluded** (Plate-Lift literals are legitimate per DESIGN.md §Elevation; either narrow the utility list to `bg|text|border|fill|stroke|ring|outline|from|via|to|decoration` or allowlist `shadow-[`).
3. **Raw color literal in `style={{...}}`**: ban a *string literal* color (`background: "oklch(...)"`, `color: "#abc"`, `background: "rgba(...)"`) but **allow** (i) an identifier/expression value (`style={{ color }}`, `style={{ background: phaseColor(x) }}`, `color-mix(...)` on a variable) and (ii) `var(--color-*)` token refs. This is the crux that separates the dozens of legit computed-phase-color sites (PhasePanel, *PhaseStrip, FocusReflectionsTable, SeriesFolioCard, PlotCard, MemberMetaRow, SpeculativeBuilder) from a real violation.
4. **Side-stripe**: `/\bborder-(l|r)-(?:4|[2-9]|\[)/` — bans `border-l-4`/`border-r-4` and `border-l-[Npx]`. Hits InfrastructureBanner:55 only (Toast:85 is inside ui/, excluded). Phase-3 redesign replaces stripes with a status-icon+label convention.

**ALLOWLIST (genuine computed color — NOT violations):**
- `src/phases.ts`, `src/lib/comparison/coloring.ts`, `src/lib/figure-export/**` (presets.ts, marks/, adapters/) — categorical/print palettes, test-pinned, are color *math sources*.
- `src/components/MemberHeatmapLayer.tsx` — `PLATE_OKLCH` feeds oklab color-mix.
- `src/components/DetectorImage.tsx` + `FocusDetectorPanel.tsx:167` — frame-edge/LUT endpoints passed as computed color props (`qRing.ts` itself has no color literals — it maps q→radius — so it needs no entry, contrary to the brief's guess; confirmed by reading it).
- `src/main.tsx:26-27` — boneyard skeleton tint config object (JS config, not className/style).
- All `style={{...}}` whose color value is an identifier/expression or `var(--color-*)`.

Implementation shape: collect violations into `{file, line, rule, snippet}`; compare against a committed `scripts/design-baseline.json`; **fail only on NEW** violations above baseline (advisory→ratchet, below). Exit 0 when ≤ baseline.

**package.json wiring:**
```json
"lint:design": "node scripts/check-design.mjs",
"build": "npm run lint:design && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.build.json && vite build"
```
(Prepend to build so a regression fails CI. During the advisory phase, `lint:design` can run with `--allow-baseline` and only print; flip to hard-fail-on-new at Phase 0 end.)

**settings.json PreToolUse hook option:** add an `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` PreToolUse matcher mirroring the existing tsc/vitest PostToolUse hooks: on a `frontend/src/*.tsx` edit, run `node scripts/check-design.mjs --file "$f" --new-only` and `exit 2` (block) if the edit introduces a NEW banned pattern not in baseline. PreToolUse runs before the write, so it can reject appearance-in-className the moment it is typed — the strongest "make it stick" lever. (Alternative: PostToolUse like the tsc hook, which lets the write land then complains; PreToolUse is preferable for a hard ban.)

## (c) Baseline + the advisory→enforcing ratchet

The `callSites` list **is** the seed `design-baseline.json` (every `text-[` with on-scale-redundant vs genuinely-off-scale marked, the 9 rounded targets, both side-stripes, the scrim/accent token sites, and the explicit ALLOWLIST so they never count). Counts: ~115 `text-[` occurrences (majority on-scale-redundant → mechanical `text-xs`/`text-sm`/`text-base`/`text-lg` swaps; a minority genuinely off-scale needing a scale extension or nearest-step decision), 9 radius targets (3 `rounded-[3px]`/`[1px]`/`[1.5px]` decorative, 3 `rounded-[7-10px]` CullBar, 6 `rounded-lg`, 4 `rounded-xl`), 1 enforced side-stripe (InfrastructureBanner).

**Ratchet protocol:**
1. **Phase 0 (advisory):** land tokens + guard + `design-baseline.json` capturing today's count. Guard runs in `build` but only **fails on counts ABOVE baseline** — no existing violation blocks, but no NEW one can be added. PreToolUse hook enforces "no new" at edit time.
2. **Per adoption PR (Phases 1–3):** each primitive adoption (SegmentedControl, PhaseChip/PhaseStrip absorbing the `rounded-[1.5px]` strips, ModalShell absorbing the `rounded-lg/xl` modals + scrim, IconButton, Card/Plate) deletes its call sites from the affected files; the PR **must regenerate and shrink** `design-baseline.json` by exactly those lines. A PR that removes violations but doesn't lower the baseline is rejected (the baseline only ratchets down). CI asserts `baseline_new <= baseline_old`.
3. **Phase 3 close:** when `design-baseline.json` reaches `[]` (every `text-[` mapped to a scale step, every off-scale radius mapped, both side-stripes converted to status-icon+label), **flip the guard to enforcing** — remove the baseline-allowance branch so ANY occurrence fails. Delete `design-baseline.json`. The side-stripe Toast (in ui/) is converted in the same wave but is not gated by the guard (ui/ excluded); it rides the PhaseStrip/status-convention work.

**Catalog scaffold note:** the guard's ui/-exclusion is what lets the catalog page demonstrate every variant/size/state with literal appearance classes if ever needed; primitives live in ui/ so they are the one place appearance is authored.

## Test plan (Vitest, RENDERED-SEMANTICS only — never class strings)
- **Tokens:** a styles.css/`@theme` assertion test (mirroring `test/phases.test.ts`'s DESIGN.md-match pattern) that pins `--radius-sm:5px`, `--radius-md:7px`, `--color-scrim` present, and `--color-print-accent === --color-accent` (resolved value equality), so a future drift is self-revealing. Assert `--radius` (singular) is GONE.
- **Guard:** unit-test `check-design.mjs` against fixture strings — `text-[10px]` flagged; `text-base` clean; `style={{ color }}` clean; `style={{ background: "oklch(...)" }}` flagged; `border-l-4` flagged; a `src/components/ui/` path excluded; an allowlisted path (phases.ts) clean; `shadow-[...rgba...]` clean. Assert baseline-diff logic: identical-to-baseline → exit 0; one extra → exit 1.
- No primitive here renders UI; the token/guard tests are config + script tests, not RTL.
migrationRisks: RADIUS SILENT SHIFT: defining --radius-sm/md changes rendered radius on 33 rounded-md + 11 rounded-sm sites at once (stock 6px→7px, 4px→5px). This is a real visual diff across the app — must be a single reviewed commit with before/after screenshots, not folded into a primitive PR.

BARE `rounded` (185 sites) is NOT covered by --radius-* in v4 (it keeps its own 0.25rem default). If the spec assumes bare rounded picks up --radius-sm, it is wrong. Decide explicitly: leave bare rounded, or sweep it to rounded-sm.

Button.tsx uses rounded-md (→7px after change) but DESIGN.md buttons spec rounded.sm/5px; the token change makes buttons 7px unless Button is also switched to rounded-sm. Don't let the token PR silently set the wrong button radius.

GUARD FALSE POSITIVES on computed color: dozens of legit `style={{ background: phaseColor(...) }}` / color-mix / var(--color-*) sites (PhasePanel, *PhaseStrip, FocusReflectionsTable, SeriesFolioCard, PlotCard, SpeculativeBuilder, MemberMetaRow).
